item.title: Python: List Comprehension vs. For Loops vs. Map/Filter/Reduce Performance
item.description:
“Python: List Comprehension vs. For Loops vs. Map/Filter/Reduce Performance”

When writing Python code, a common consideration is performance. Specifically, how do constructs like list comprehensions stack up against traditional for loops, or functional programming tools such as map, filter, and reduce? While general guidelines exist, actual performance can depend on the specific use case and even the Python version.

Let’s delve into the nuances and see what the community’s experience and benchmarks reveal.

item.title: C++ Guaranteed Copy Elision Explained: Return Value Optimization
item.description:
“C++ Guaranteed Copy Elision Explained: Return Value Optimization”

How does C++ handle copy elision, particularly in the context of return value optimization (RVO), and what changed with C++17’s guaranteed copy elision for prvalues?

Copy elision is a compiler optimization that avoids unnecessary copying or moving of objects. In C++, this can occur in several scenarios, most notably when returning objects from functions. Before C++17, copy elision was permitted but not guaranteed. This meant that even if the compiler elided a copy or move operation, the object type still needed to support accessible copy or move constructors.
